## Proof

Recall that two embeddings $f, g: M \to N$ are **diffeotopic** if there exists a diffeotopy of $N$: a smooth map $H: N \times [0,1] \to N$ such that $H_0 = \mathrm{id}_N$, each $H_t := H(\cdot, t)$ is a diffeomorphism of $N$, and $g = H_1 \circ f$.

Since $H_1: N \to N$ is a diffeomorphism, it is in particular a homeomorphism. Moreover, $H_1$ maps $f(M)$ onto $g(M)$, since for every $p \in M$,
$$H_1(f(p)) = (H_1 \circ f)(p) = g(p).$$

Because $H_1$ is a bijection of $N$ that sends $f(M)$ onto $g(M)$, it sends the complement $N \setminus f(M)$ onto $N \setminus g(M)$. The restriction
$$H_1\big|_{N \setminus f(M)} : N \setminus f(M) \;\longrightarrow\; N \setminus g(M)$$
is a homeomorphism (a restriction of a homeomorphism to an invariant subset, with image the corresponding invariant subset).

Connectedness is a topological invariant. Since $N \setminus f(M)$ is connected by hypothesis and $N \setminus g(M)$ is homeomorphic to it, $N \setminus g(M)$ is also connected. $\blacksquare$
